title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Problem (E526, the section on a rod pinned at both ends E and F and also pinned by a stylus at an interior point L): the length is scaled to 1, EL = λ and LF = 1−λ. Each span's mode shape is a combination of e^{±ωx}, sin ωx and cos ωx, with frequency proportional to ω². The pin conditions at E and F give β = −α and β' = −α'e^{2ω}. Zero deflection at L gives γ and γ'. The previous page derives two equations at L. III is moment/curvature continuity. IV is slope continuity: α(e^{λω}−e^{−λω}) = α'(e^{λω}−e^{ω(2−λ)}).

On this page Euler solves IV by setting α = e^{λω}−e^{ω(2−λ)} = −2e^{ω} sinh((1−λ)ω) and α' = 2 sinh λω. Substituting into III gives the frequency equation
0 = 2 − 2e^{2ω} − αα'(cot λω + cot(1−λ)ω).
Since cot a + cot b = sin(a+b)/(sin a sin b), this equals the second form 0 = 2 − 2e^{2ω} − αα' sin ω/(sin λω sin(1−λ)ω).

Modern form: write a = λω and b = (1−λ)ω. Then 2 − 2e^{2ω} = −4e^{ω} sinh ω, and αα' = −4e^{ω} sinh a sinh b. The equation becomes sinh(a+b)/(sinh a sinh b) = cot a + cot b. That is coth a + coth b = cot a + cot b, or
(coth a − cot a) + (coth b − cot b) = 0.
This is the standard frequency equation of a two-span continuous Euler–Bernoulli beam on three simple supports.

Euler declines to solve it for general λ ('formulas tantopere complicatas'). He says it suffices to have given the method. He then examines the limits λ→0 and λ→1, claiming only rest (ω = 0) survives. He announces that the case λ = 1/2 deserves separate treatment. On the next page that case factors into sin(ω/2) = 0 (antisymmetric modes, each half pinned–pinned) and tan(ω/2) = tanh(ω/2) (symmetric modes, each half clamped–pinned).
errors: The λ→0 limit is mishandled. Euler sets α' = e^{λω} − e^{−λω} = 0 but ignores that cot λω (equivalently 1/sin λω) diverges. The product α'·cot λω → 2 has a finite limit, so the bracketed term does not vanish. The correct limit makes the equation tend to coth ω − cot ω = 0, i.e. tan ω = tanh ω. This is the clamped–pinned frequency equation. The true limit is not 0 = 2(1 − e^{2ω}) with only ω = 0.

Physically, two pins infinitely close together act as a clamp. The remaining span therefore still vibrates as a clamped–pinned beam, and the conclusion 'nullum motum ... status quietis' is wrong. The same holds for λ→1. Euler even notes that F is then 'quasi muro infixus' (built into a wall), yet still concludes rest; that remark points to the correct answer.
Minor: on the previous page's transcription, δ' is missing an 'e' ('α'(^{λω}…').

ideas.what: Frequency equation of a beam simply supported at both ends with an intermediate simple support at arbitrary position λ.
ideas.modern_name: Two-span continuous beam frequency equation: (coth a − cot a) + (coth b − cot b) = 0
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in 19th–20th c. vibration literature (Rayleigh-era and later engineering texts on continuous beams); Euler's E526 discussed by Truesdell (1960)
ideas.where_published: E526, Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1779 (publ. 1782); surveyed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II.11.2)

ideas.what: Simplifying cot λω + cot(1−λ)ω = sin ω/(sin λω sin(1−λ)ω).
Analysis of the limiting support positions λ = 0 and λ = 1 (support approaching an end).
ideas.modern_name: Limit of coalescing supports producing a clamped end

missed.claim: Euler's limit analysis is wrong. As the intermediate support approaches an end, the frequency equation tends to tan ω = tanh ω (clamped–pinned), not to rest. Euler's own remark that the end becomes 'quasi muro infixus' anticipates the correct interpretation, but the 0·∞ limit was mishandled.
missed.quote: patet, si fuerit λ = 0 ... nullum motum communem inter ambas partes existere posse, id quod etiam calculus ostendet, quippe qui praebet 0 = 2(1 − e^{2ω})
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of historical interest: it documents an error in E526 that commentaries may or may not flag. The physics is well known.

missed.claim: The general-λ frequency equation is left unsolved. Euler does not reach the symmetric form (coth a − cot a) + (coth b − cot b) = 0, which would have made numerical treatment easy.
missed.quote: quem quidem laborem, ob formulas tantopere complicatas, suscipere non ausim
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: No real gap: the equation was later solved and tabulated in engineering literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page gives a correct and fairly early form of the two-span beam frequency equation. This is known content of E526, discussed by Truesdell. The only notable finding is the mishandled λ→0 limit, a minor error rather than a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: 'δ' = α'(^{λω} − ...' should read 'α'(e^{λω} − e^{ω(2−λ)})'.
This page's transcription matches the image; in the image, 'cot.λω + cot.(1−λ)ω' has the plus sign printed somewhat faintly.
